summary: The Urban Health Transformation Act of 2026 establishes a federal program administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to provide funding and support to states for improving urban health care access, outcomes, and facility stability.

key_provisions: Appropriates $10 billion annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to the Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for state allotments.
Appropriates $200 million for fiscal year 2026 for implementing the program.

Requires states to submit an approved urban health transformation plan focusing on access, health outcomes, emerging technologies, strategic partnerships, workforce recruitment, and financial solvency of urban hospitals.

Distributes 50 percent of annual funds equally among all eligible states with approved applications and 50 percent based on factors including urban population proportions and numbers of urban health facilities.
Prohibits states from requiring matching funds to receive allotments.
Limits state administrative expenses to no more than 10 percent of their annual allotment.

Directs that state funds be used for at least three of ten specified health-related activities, such as chronic disease management, workforce recruitment, technology upgrades, and mental health or substance use disorder services.
missing_information: Specific formulas or weightings the Administrator will use for the 50 percent variable portion of state allotments.
Detailed criteria the Administrator will use to evaluate state urban health transformation plans.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Urban Health Transformation Act of 2026 establishes a federal program administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to provide funding and support to states for improving urban health care access, outcomes, and facility stability.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a multi-billion dollar federal grant program dedicated specifically to urban health systems, directing $50 billion over five years to states and urban health facilities to address hospital closures, workforce shortages, technology gaps, and care delivery models. The significance score is 85.
